thread.title_full: Honorary Street Sign Sparks Bitter Clash - NewsBreak

author: Sarah Bennett
title: Honorary Street Sign Sparks Bitter Clash - NewsBreak
text:
By Sarah Bennett ,
31 minutes ago Christian minister Edward “Ted” Barham and Dearborn Mayor Abdullah Hammoud clashed over whether to grant honorary street signs recognizing Arab American News publisher Osama Siblani. The controversy stemmed from past quotes attributed to Siblani, which critics claimed show sympathy toward groups designated as terrorist organizations. Barham objected to the honorary signs after reading remarks attributed to Osama Siblani, prompting Mayor Abdullah Hammoud to tell Barham he was “not welcome” in Dearborn.
Barham said, “I did not respond to the mayor with hate. I said, God bless you.” He then cited the Bible’s call to “love your enemies, bless those who curse you.”
Siblani disputed the context of the excerpts and criticized the organizations compiling them. He previously stated, “We are the Arabs who are going to lift Palestinians all the way to victory whether we are in Michigan and whether we are in Jenin.”
Siblani added, “Believe me, everyone should fight within his means. They will fight with stones, others will fight with guns, others fight with planes, drones, and rockets.”
Hammoud’s statement toward Barham drew local criticism. Barham noted that he will continue promoting Christian expression in public spaces.
The Anti-Defamation League (ADL) and MEMRI documented quotations attributed to Siblani that had drawn scrutiny. Siblani argued some quotes were taken out of context.
ADL quoted Siblani stating, “If the FBI wants to come after those who support the resistance done by Hezbollah, then they better bring a fleet of buses. I, for one, would be willing to go to jail.”
In 2003, Siblani stated, “[George W. Bush] believes Hezbollah, Hamas and other Palestinian factions are terrorists, but we believe they are freedom fighters.”
Michigan Gov. Gretchen Whitmer has refrained from publicly addressing the issue.
Sarah Bennett covers U.S. politics & news for content partner Modern Newsstand LLC.
